explanation: This slide describes energy flow pathways and trophic structures. A food web represents the interconnected networks of energy flow within an ecosystem, consisting of two main types: grazing food webs, which begin with primary producers, and detrital food webs, which begin with decomposers. Food chains depict single, straight-line feeding relationships. Trophic levels indicate the nutrient/energy level of organisms within a food chain, moving from producers to primary consumers, secondary consumers, and so on. An ecological pyramid illustrates the energy loss between these trophic levels, where typically only about 10% of the energy is successfully transferred to the next level. Biomass is calculated as the number of organisms at a trophic level multiplied by their individual weight.

questions.q: What is the difference between a grazing food web and a detrital food web?
opts: Grazing food webs start with decomposers, while detrital food webs start with predators.
Grazing food webs start with producers, while detrital food webs start with decomposers.
Grazing food webs exist only in water, while detrital food webs are terrestrial.
There is no difference; they are synonymous terms.
questions.exp: The notes state that the 'Grazing food web starts with producers' and the 'Detrital food web starts with decomposers.'

questions.q: What percentage of energy is typically transferred from one trophic level to the next in an ecological pyramid?
questions.exp: According to the notes, an ecological pyramid shows energy losses between trophic levels, and 'Normally only ~ 10% energy makes it to next level.'

questions.q: How is biomass defined in the context of this slide?
opts: The volume of organic matter divided by the total area of the ecosystem
The number of organisms at each trophic level multiplied by their weight
The speed at which producers convert sunlight into chemical energy
The chemical energy stored in reservoirs unavailable to producers
